title: Zone-refined access pillars sweep deep-trap metals into a sacrificial cap
idea: Borrow ingot zone refining: scan a nanosecond-laser molten zone up each vertical access-transistor pillar topped with a sacrificial a-Si cap, so Fe/Cu/Ni deep-level impurities (segregation coefficient k<<1) ride the melt front into the cap, which CMP then removes.
why: Fact 3: the <=13 fA tail is set by rare cells hosting SRH deep traps; purging them could cut tail cells ~10x, pushing worst-case retention toward 0.5-1 s and cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss by up to ~80%.

title: Veneer-peeled single-crystal foils give every 3D tier bulk-grade transistors
idea: Like a rotary veneer lathe peeling a log, repeatedly cleave 30-50 nm single-crystal Si foils from one reusable donor boule (H-implant plus stressor-controlled spalling) and bond them tier by tier, so each of 26+ tiers gets bulk-quality lateral access transistors with no Si/SiGe superlattice epi and no poly-Si.
why: Fact 2 (lateral transistor blocker): single-crystal channels avoid poly grain-boundary leakage (~100x lower tail) in every tier, and donor reuse keeps cost per tier to a bond plus cleave step.

title: Millefiori glass-cane draw sliced into litho-free vertical access arrays
idea: Assemble a cm-scale preform holding ~10^4 coaxial access-transistor cross-sections (chalcogenide-glass semiconductor core, glass gate dielectric, low-melting metal gate). Thermally draw it 10^4x as Venetian millefiori cane or optical fiber is drawn, then slice 100 nm discs: each slice is a ready-made array of vertical gate-all-around access switches.
why: Capital intensity and fact 4: removes the EUV patterning of the access layer altogether. A wide-gap glassy channel gives low off-current, and one draw tower replaces scanners for this layer.

title: Automotive e-coat bath self-plugs capacitor dielectric pinholes
idea: Before the top electrode goes on, immerse the array in an electrophoretic polymer/oxide paint bath and bias the bottom electrodes. Only pinholes and thin spots conduct, so insulating deposit grows exactly there and stops itself, just as car-body e-coat seals only the exposed metal.
why: Retention tail from dielectric leakage: plugging the weak spots could cut those tail cells ~5x and allow ~10-15% thinner high-k for more Cs at the same leakage.

title: Plywood cross-grain laminated channels break grain-boundary leakage paths
idea: Build the poly channel of 3D/BEOL access transistors as 3-5 ultrathin plies with rotated texture and amorphous seams between them, so grain boundaries never line up through the film. This copies the way plywood crosses its grain to stop through-splits.
why: Off-state tail in poly-Si or poly-oxide channels is set by the worst percolating GB path. Misaligned plies could cut the tail ~10x while on-current still flows along the plies.

title: Lost-wax helical channel packs a 60 nm gate into 12 nm footprint
idea: Deposit a sacrificial carbon helix in the pillar hole by glancing-angle spiral deposition, wrap it with gate dielectric and metal, burn the carbon out (lost-wax casting), then ALD-backfill the helical void with the channel. The result is a gate-all-around helix with L~60 nm in a vertical cell.
why: Fact 3: long L kills DIBL and short-channel subthreshold leakage by orders of magnitude, so VT can be lowered and wordline voltage dropped (fact 10) while retention rises ~10x. The cost is on-current, offset by the GAA helix width.

title: Ceramic-glazed wide-gap heterojunction skin on the storage-node junction
idea: Like a glaze fired onto pottery, grow a 2-3 nm lattice-matched wide-gap crystal skin (e.g., GaP or AlP on Si, Eg ~2.3-2.5 eV) only on the storage-node side of the access channel. Band-to-band tunneling and GIDL must then cross a wide gap.
why: GIDL is a dominant tail mechanism under high storage voltage and wordline-low bias. BTBT falls roughly with exp(-Eg^1.5), so >100x less GIDL leakage could stretch refresh intervals several-fold.

title: Solar-cell fixed-charge passivation spacer on the storage junction
idea: Borrow PERC/TOPCon solar-cell field-effect passivation: put a SiNx/AlOx spacer with engineered fixed charge (positive next to the n+ storage node) over the storage-junction surface. The surface stays accumulated, so surface SRH generation and the GIDL fringe field are suppressed.
why: The solar industry cut surface recombination velocity ~100x this way. Here it targets the surface-generation share of junction leakage, aiming for a 3-5x tail reduction with tools already in high-volume solar fabs.

title: Bearing-style selective assembly pairs leaky arrays with tight sense amps
idea: In a CMOS-bonded-array flow, map each array wafer's retention and each periphery wafer's sense-amp offset before hybrid bonding. Then pair dies by measurement, as bearing makers match graded balls to races, so the leakiest arrays get the lowest-offset sense amps.
why: Retention spec equals charge loss vs sense margin. Matched pairing could lift the worst-case refresh interval ~1.5-2x and raise sellable yield without any process change.

title: Basket-weave buried wordlines dive and rise to starve passing-gate leakage
idea: Route each buried wordline over-and-under like basket weave: it runs deep beside one storage node and shallow beside the next. No storage node then sits beside a full-depth passing gate whose toggling pumps electrons into it.
why: Facts 3 and 9: passing-gate-induced charge loss is a leakage mechanism behind row hammer. Weave geometry could raise the hammer threshold ~5-10x and remove most targeted-refresh overhead.

title: Accordion-folded single membrane becomes 26 tiers of crystalline cells
idea: Process one planar single-crystal membrane (SOI device layer) with lateral access transistors in a strip pattern, release it, then fold it accordion-style like a road map using prestressed hinge lines. N folds yield N tiers that all came from one high-quality planar process.
why: Fact 2: gives 3D DRAM single-crystal lateral transistors for every tier while using only planar processing once. Folding replaces 26x deposition/etch loops.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembled 3 nm nanowires widen bandgap by confinement
idea: Use block-copolymer self-assembly (no litho) to define 3-4 nm vertical Si nanowire access channels. Quantum confinement raises the effective gap to ~1.6-2 eV, exponentially suppressing BTBT/GIDL and intrinsic generation.
why: Facts 3 and 4: wider effective gap could cut junction/GIDL leakage 10-100x and removes an EUV layer. Series resistance and diameter variability are the risks.

title: Fermented bacterial S-layer protein crystals as access-pillar etch masks
idea: Ferment bacteria whose surface-layer proteins self-crystallize into 2D lattices with ~10-13 nm period. Harvest and transfer these sheets onto the wafer as hard-mask templates for the vertical access-pillar array.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4): replaces 1-2 EUV or multi-patterning steps with a bioreactor. Atomically identical protein pores tighten pillar diameter, so VT and leakage spread narrow and the tail shrinks.

title: Float-glass style liquid-gallium printing of atomically thin Ga2O3 channels
idea: As float glass forms on molten tin, kiss the wafer against a liquid Ga/In alloy. Its self-limiting 1.5-3 nm oxide skin transfers at room temperature as a crystalline wide-gap 2D channel for BEOL access transistors.
why: Eg ~4.8 eV in an atomically thin channel could push off-current below 1e-21 A per cell (beyond IGZO). It is BEOL-stackable for 3D with no epitaxy tool, aiming for >100x less refresh.

title: Andon-cord canary cells trigger refresh only when truly needed
idea: Each subarray carries a few deliberately weak canary cells (thinner Cs or a leakier spacer), sensed continuously by a tiny comparator. Like a Toyota andon cord, a tripped canary pulls refresh for that subarray only, tracking real temperature and VRT state.
why: Fact 3: replaces the fixed 64/32 ms guardband with measured need, plausibly 2-4x fewer refreshes and matching recovered bandwidth.

title: Wordline hot-wire annealing heals retention in the field
idea: Periodically drive a calibrated current pulse through a wordline segment, as hot-wire annealing or blade tempering does, to flash-heat the gate stack to ~300-400 C for microseconds. The pulse re-passivates interface traps and resets VRT defects that grew during service.
why: Retention degradation over life and VRT: restoring the tail ~2x late in life avoids derating refresh rates and extends module service life.

title: Hot-isostatic-press deuterium loads buried channels of deep 3D stacks
idea: Borrow HIP, which closes casting voids: 20-100 atm D2 at ~350 C forces deuterium through 26+ tiers to passivate dangling bonds in buried lateral channels that ordinary forming gas never reaches. Deuterium's mass also resists hot-carrier depassivation.
why: Fact 2/3: equalizes the leakage tail between top and bottom tiers of 3D DRAM, plausibly 2-5x in deep tiers.

title: Coin-minting nanoimprint strikes the access-pillar layer instead of EUV
idea: Write one master die by e-beam, replicate working stamps, and strike the access-pillar layer by nanoimprint like coin minting. A reverse-tone, self-aligned spacer step reaches sub-12 nm pillars.
why: Fact 4: removes 1-2 EUV exposures from the access device module. Imprint's low line-edge roughness tightens VT spread and so trims the leakage tail.

title: Cleanroom-airlock double gate splits voltage across two stacked channels
idea: Put two independent gates on the same vertical pillar with a floating middle node, like a cleanroom airlock with two doors. In hold, the middle node settles mid-rail, so each channel sees half the Vds.
why: Subthreshold (DIBL) and GIDL leakage are exponential in Vds. The stack effect gives 10-100x lower off-current at zero added footprint in a vertical cell.

title: Retread DRAM: remanufactured modules sold with per-row retention maps
idea: Like tire retreading, take DRAM from decommissioned servers, re-characterize each row's retention at temperature, and write the map into the SPD. Resell the modules for tiers whose controllers apply per-row refresh rates.
why: Raises usable supply during shortage. Per-row refresh on mapped modules cuts refresh energy 2-4x versus blanket rates.

title: Galvanized sacrificial hydrogen reservoir re-passivates traps over lifetime
idea: Place a hydrogen-rich SiNx:H liner next to the access channel as a galvanizing-style sacrificial layer. It slowly releases H to re-passivate interface traps as they depassivate in service, much as zinc corrodes first to protect steel.
why: Lifetime retention drift and VRT growth: keeps the tail near time-zero quality, avoiding end-of-life refresh-rate derating.

title: Laser-trimmed wordline-low voltage per subarray at its leakage minimum
idea: Like laser-trimming thin-film resistors to spec, measure each subarray's leakage vs negative-wordline voltage at wafer test. Fuse-trim each subarray's VNWL and body bias to the bottom of its own V-shaped curve, the balance of subthreshold against GIDL.
why: The optimum wordline-low shifts by a few hundred mV across a die. Per-subarray trimming could cut tail leakage 2-5x at almost no area.

title: Furnace refractory lining: thermal break shields HBM from hot logic
idea: Like a refractory firebrick lining, insert a low-k porous thermal-break layer between the logic base die and the DRAM stack. Logic heat is routed around the DRAM through peripheral copper thermal columns to the lid.
why: Leakage roughly doubles every ~10 C. Keeping HBM 20 C cooler cuts refresh rate ~4x and lifts bandwidth.

title: Glassblown vacuum-tube nanochannel access switch canned in every cell
idea: Hermetically seal a ~10 nm vacuum gap between a sharpened bitline emitter and a metal storage node, with a surrounding gate electrode, like miniature canned vacuum tubes. Charge moves only by field emission when the gate lowers the barrier.
why: Zero refresh: no semiconductor means no SRH, GIDL or junction leakage, and a junctionless MIM node with thick dielectric leaks <1e-23 A. Retention exceeds years, so refresh is eliminated.

title: Stamped snap-dome nanobeam stores bits as buckled up or down
idea: Like keyboard snap domes stamped from prestressed sheet, each cell is a prestressed nanobeam buckled up or down, flipped electrostatically in ns and read capacitively. Contact-free flexing avoids wear.
why: Zero refresh: the bit is mechanical shape, not charge, so nothing leaks. Zero standby and refresh power, with GHz-resonator-class flexures able to reach high endurance.

title: Over-center toggle-clamp NEMS relay isolates a junctionless MIM node
idea: The access device is a nano-relay with over-center (toggle-clamp) geometry: it latches open with no hold voltage and leaves a true air gap between bitline and a metal storage capacitor that has no pn junction.
why: Zero refresh: an open air gap conducts nothing, and with no junction only dielectric leakage remains (<1e-22 A), so charge persists for months or years. Contact wear is the honest risk.

title: Lab-grown-gem CVD diamond access transistors with 5.5 eV channels
idea: Reuse the U.S. lab-grown diamond industry's CVD reactors to grow thin single-crystal diamond tiers. Build H-terminated surface-channel access FETs on them, using transfer-doping oxide such as MoO3 to switch the channel on.
why: Zero refresh: intrinsic generation in 5.5 eV diamond is effectively nil and junctionless surface channels remove GIDL, giving retention of years. This also creates a domestic, non-EUV memory supply chain.

title: Supermarket expiry dating places perishable data in unrefreshed banks
idea: OS/runtime allocators tag buffers with a use-by time, as a supermarket dates perishables. Activations, KV-cache pages, packet buffers and staging tensors go to banks with refresh permanently disabled whose certified retention (e.g., 250 ms at 85 C) exceeds the tag. Expired data is recomputed or re-fetched.
why: Zero refresh power for the perishable share of capacity, often a large fraction of AI accelerator memory. It recovers the 10-20% refresh bandwidth there.

title: Assembly-line takt sweep: every row restored by normal reads
idea: Set the memory controller's address mapping and scheduler so streaming workloads (LLM weight sweeps, frame buffers) activate every row within a takt time below tREFW. Disable refresh and verify coverage with a per-row activation bitmap.
why: Zero refresh power: restore happens as a free side effect of reads that occur anyway. Fits HBM in inference, where weights are swept every token.

title: Dairy cold-chain milk-run delivers LN2 to cryogenic memory pods
idea: Put capacity-memory sleds in sealed 77 K dewar pods topped up by scheduled liquid-nitrogen deliveries, like a dairy milk-run. Industrial LN2 is a by-product of oxygen plants, so no on-site compressor is needed.
why: Zero refresh power: at 77 K, access-transistor leakage falls by >10 orders of magnitude and retention runs from hours to days, so refresh is disabled. CV^2 energy and wire resistance also drop.

title: Newspaper-press model ROM: reprint inference weights each release
idea: Store frozen inference weights in via- or imprint-programmed mask ROM printed on mature U.S. nodes, reprinted per model release like a newspaper edition. It is byte-addressable at ~10-20 ns behind the accelerator.
why: Zero refresh: printed vias never leak. It removes the largest read-only consumer of HBM/DRAM capacity at a fraction of the cost per bit, with no EUV.

title: Ripstop Z-channel codes let decayed ones be woven back
idea: Like ripstop nylon's reinforcing threads stopping tears, encode rows with asymmetric Z-channel / constant-weight codes built for one-way 1->0 decay. Leaked ones become known-direction erasures that are corrected and rewritten on read.
why: Zero refresh for data read within the extended window: the usable unrefreshed lifetime grows from ~64 ms to several seconds, covering most transient AI data with no refresh energy.

title: Watch-detent Goto pair of tunnel diodes holds each node
idea: Like a watch escapement detent, each storage node is the midpoint of two series tunnel diodes (Goto pair) whose N-shaped I-V curves give two stable voltages. The node self-restores to 0 or 1 at only the diodes' valley current.
why: Zero refresh power: the cell self-latches, so no refresh cycles or sense restores are needed. With pA-class valley currents, total hold power can fall below today's refresh energy.

title: Locksmith combination-lock access: resonant-tunneling barrier opens only at key bias
idea: Replace the gated transistor with a double-barrier resonant-tunneling stack (e.g., AlN/GaN wells) between bitline and storage well. Charge passes only when the bitline bias aligns the quantized level, like a key cut to one combination. Off-resonance, thick wide-gap barriers block flow.
why: Zero refresh: off-resonance transmission and thermionic leakage over ~2 eV barriers give retention of years, and energy-selective access needs no gate oxide or junction.

title: E-ink microcapsule bit: charged nanoparticle parked top or bottom
idea: Scale e-paper microcapsule manufacturing to a sealed ~10 nm cage holding one charged nanoparticle or ion cluster, held by image-charge adhesion to the top or bottom electrode. It is moved by a field pulse and read by capacitance difference.
why: Zero refresh: position is held by adhesion with no leaking charge and no hold power. The ns transit over 10 nm in vacuum is the speculative part.

title: Plumbing check-valve pair: ultra-high-barrier Schottky diodes guard the node
idea: Isolate each metal storage node with two back-to-back high-barrier Schottky rectifiers (e.g., Pt/Ga2O3, ~1.8 eV) to separate write-high and write-low lines, like check valves cast into a pipe tee. Pulsing the line past the barrier fills or drains the node.
why: Zero refresh: thermionic reverse leakage over a 1.8 eV barrier is ~1e-30 A per cell, so retention exceeds the product's life. A two-terminal access device also removes the transistor and simplifies the wordline.

title: Laminated-glass hBN floating-graphene bit with sub-ns super-injection
idea: Like safety glass laminated around a PVB interlayer, stack a graphene charge layer between hBN tunnel barriers over a 2D MoS2 channel. Writes use the 2D-enhanced hot-carrier super-injection that reaches sub-ns programming, so the cell is read like a gain cell.
why: Zero refresh: charge behind 6 eV hBN stays for years. The open question is DRAM-class endurance, so the risk is honestly high.

title: Nitinol-stent style ferroelastic twin variants store bits as strain
idea: Borrow shape-memory-alloy training: a nanoscale ferroelastic or martensitic island is trained to two twin variants (strain orientations). A gate-adjacent piezo or electrostatic pulse flips it, and a piezoresistive channel underneath reads it.
why: Zero refresh: crystallographic twin state is non-volatile without charge storage. It differs from ferroelectric and MRAM routes and avoids leakage physics entirely.

title: Day-old bread pricing: discounted refresh-disabled perishable-memory cloud SKU
idea: Cloud providers sell refresh-disabled DRAM capacity at a discount, the way bakeries sell day-old bread. It comes with a retention SLA (e.g., data valid for 200 ms after its last write) for batch shuffles, caches and inference scratch. Hypervisors map it to unrefreshed banks.
why: Zero refresh power on that capacity. It creates a market price signal that turns refresh-free operation into extra usable supply during the shortage.

title: USDA-style retention grade stamp and JEDEC refresh-optional mode
idea: Like USDA grading stamps on meat and eggs, require every DRAM die to carry a tested retention grade (e.g., R1 >= 250 ms, R2 >= 2 s at 85 C) and standardize a JEDEC mode that disables refresh per bank. Software can then target refresh-free placement.
why: Zero refresh power deployable at scale: makes refresh-disabled operation a standard, verifiable product attribute instead of a lab trick.

title: Wire-drawn superconducting persistent-current loops for cryogenic working memory
idea: Use superconducting wire-drawing know-how (NbTi/Nb3Sn) as thin-film Nb micro-loops where the bit is a circulating persistent current. Josephson-junction access switches write and read it at 4 K, next to quantum computers and cryo-CMOS.
why: Zero refresh: persistent currents never decay and junction-based access has no leakage, so refresh and hold power are both zero. This serves cryogenic compute without a warm-DRAM round trip.

title: Sand-mold disposable cache: DRAM copies decay, nonvolatile pattern persists
idea: Like sand-casting molds broken after each pour while the pattern is kept, treat DRAM as a cache of clean lines backed by a dense nonvolatile master. Each line carries a restore timestamp. Lines past their certified retention are silently invalidated as misses instead of refreshed.
why: Zero refresh power. Capacity is spent only on lines being used, so DRAM needed per workload falls and the cost is an occasional refill from backing storage.

title: Coin-cell nanobattery bit holds voltage as state of charge
idea: Shrink coin-cell battery manufacturing to a solid-state Li-free nanobattery per cell (e.g., proton or Ag+ intercalation electrodes). The bit is its open-circuit voltage, read non-destructively through a gain transistor and written by a short current pulse.
why: Zero refresh: a battery holds its voltage for years by electrochemistry, not by isolating charge. Speed and endurance are the speculative risks.

title: Micrometer-screw tunneling-gap shutter switches without any contact
idea: A nanocantilever, positioned like a precision micrometer screw, moves the bitline electrode from a 0.5 nm tunnel gap (on) to a 3 nm gap (off) above a metal storage node. It never touches, so there is no stiction or contact wear.
why: Zero refresh: tunneling current falls ~exp(-2kd), about 10^10x from on to off, so off-leakage drops below 1e-24 A and retention lasts years. The non-contact design improves endurance over relays.

title: Cookie-cutter procedural data regenerated from seeds instead of stored
idea: Like stamping cookies from a cutter instead of storing them, replace stored tensors that are pseudo-random or structured (random projections, initializations, LoRA bases, positional tables, dropout masks) with seeds plus near-memory generators. These recreate each line at access time.
why: Zero refresh: data that is never stored never needs refresh. It also cuts the DRAM footprint and data-movement energy (fact 5) for that share of memory.

title: Kiln-shrunk silicon dots make a Coulomb-blockade multi-junction access chain
idea: Like clay shrinking in a kiln, use self-limiting oxidation to shrink Si islands to ~1.5 nm, forming a chain of 4-6 tunnel junctions between bitline and storage node. The chain's Coulomb blockade is lifted only when the side gate is pulsed.
why: Zero refresh: cotunneling leakage falls exponentially with junction count, giving retention of days to years at room temperature with no semiconductor junction to leak.
